newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: A stronger rand and bond market during the afternoon pushed South African industrial shares into firmer territory after a weak start.
Gold stocks fell for the sixth consecutive session but ended off the day's weakest levels on perceptions that the $354-an-ounce level on bullion offered strong resistance.
"After lunch the rand and gilts market improved a lot and some confidence flowed back into the share market," one dealer said.

The rand jumped to its best level against the dollar in five weeks, touching a best bid of 4.6440, on a stream of offshore dollar sales. But the local currency retraced most of its gains towards the close as players took profits.
"It was a volatile day (on all markets)," a dealer said.
Industrials initially started weak following a 51-point fall on Wall Street on Wednesday night and hefty falls on the Japanese stock market on Thursday.
But traders said investment funds returned to the market by late morning, continuing a trend started on Wednesday, buying cheap stocks. However, some funds were also seen selling stocks.
"There was some natural selling in the market too, mainly from funds," a trader said.

The industrial index ended up 18.7 points at 8,020.1 with SA Breweries up 75 cents at 120.25 rand, Nedcor rising 100 cents to 115.50 rand, Remgro gaining 20 cents to 42 rand but Investec shed 100 cents to 115.50 rand.
Industrials were expected firm again on Friday, although eyeing Wall Street overnight for any further heavy falls. "The (local) market looks like it wants to go better," a dealer said.

On the gold board stocks ended at fresh one year lows as bullion continued to look sickly. Shares have so far ended weaker every day this year, but traders said some good buying was evident at the lower levels.
"Some people are closing short positions. I'd say that accounts for about 75 percent of buying," a trader said.
Some felt bullion had bottomed out for the time being.
"$354 has always been a major resistance. People are betting that it will not break."
The all gold index finished 8.6 points down at 1390.1 with Freegold off five cents at 32.20 rand, Western Areas 100 cents weaker at 60 rand, but Vaal Reefs lifted 400 cents to 282 rand.
The all share index was down 3.3 points at 6,647.9.
Dealers said volumes had returned to normal levels after a quiet holiday and early new year period with shares worth 568 million rand trading on Thursday.

On the equity futures market contracts were slightly firmer in late trading boosted by the rand and expectations of a stronger Wall Street on Thursday after the release of non-inflationary U.S. PPI data.
The March industrial contract was at 7,912/20 from 7,876, the gold contract at 980/995 from 973 and the all-share contract at 6,212/25 from 6,211.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
